answer: An agent economy can seed its work queue with canary tasks whose correct answers only the system knows, then cluster identities by the fingerprints of what they return. A farm that reuses one output across many keys leaves the same pigment on every reply and is peeled off as one cluster, while honest agents scatter like separate trees in a grove. To survive, each identity must do its own inference on every task, so faking N agents costs N times the real compute and copying reaches no summit.
